summary: Configured node1 so only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs. The configuration and cron service remained healthy after a verified node restart; the CentOS release, kernel, and installed Cronie version were preserved.
actions_performed: Created the missing opsadmin account without setting credentials.
Created /etc/cron.allow containing exactly root and opsadmin, owned by root:root with mode 0600.
Verified root and opsadmin can install crontabs while nobody is rejected.
Removed all temporary crontabs, backups, and test artifacts.
Safely restarted node1 and verified its boot identity changed.
Confirmed crond, accounts, access controls, and authorization behavior recovered after restart.

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: Shows the exact protected allowlist, successful crontab installation for root and opsadmin, explicit rejection of nobody, and clean final state.
Proves opsadmin was created and persisted through restart.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: CentOS Stream 10, kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64, and the existing Cronie 1.7.0 package remained unchanged.

Captures the healthy baseline and original boot ID, acknowledged safe reboot, observed outage, changed boot ID, recovered crond service and allowlist, post-restart functional authorization test, and final clean health state.
